A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MoDGS and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The earlier material can be matched across versions, including Appendices A.1–A.14; v3 adds A.15–A.20.

before.justification: v2 reports original rendering experiments, quantitative benchmark comparisons, and ablations in Tables 1–11 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative loss and depth-estimator comparisons plus qualitative depth-quality and motion evaluations.

M1.justification: The canonical Gaussians, invertible deformation network, 3D-aware initialization, ordinal depth loss, and training procedure remain unchanged. Alternative losses and depth estimators are experimental variants; the new adaptive-fusion suggestion in Section 3.2 is prospective.

E1.justification: The four named datasets remain unchanged. Appendix A.18 adds the DAVIS rollerblade rapid-motion/motion-blur scenario. The new depth-quality comparison uses Camel and Bear, already represented in Figure 11; the complex-motion examples also reuse existing NVIDIA scenes.

E2.justification: v3 adds NVDS as an evaluated depth-quality comparator in Figure 16 and an LPIPS depth-loss alternative in Table 12. Existing rendering baselines, Shape-of-Motion, and earlier loss comparisons remain. ChronoDepth matches the Shao et al. method already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: New controlled experiments replace ordinal supervision with an AlexNet-based LPIPS loss and vary the depth estimator while holding other configurations fixed (A.16 and A.20). Existing camera splits, metrics, scale alignment, and training budgets remain unchanged; these additions do not establish reruns of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: A.15–A.18 and A.20 substantially expand supplementary analysis: depth quality against NVDS, perceptual versus ordinal supervision, complex and rapid-motion case studies, and robustness across depth estimators. These test additional questions beyond the retained initialization, noise, ranking-loss, and video-depth ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new tables retain point-estimate reporting. Gaussian-noise parameters in the existing robustness experiment are perturbation settings, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 retain their numerical results, but Tables 12–13 and Figures 13–17 substantially extend the reported evidence. Table 12 adds sear-steak PSNR of 22.43 with LPIPS supervision versus 23.53 with ordinal supervision; Table 13 reports PSNR ranging from 23.12 to 23.44 across depth estimators. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v2 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the ordinal-loss definition, and the Pearson/normalized-depth equivalence derivation in A.5 are retained. The new distillation interpretation and explicit depth-order limitation introduce no new formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: casual monocular dynamic view synthesis through 3D-aware initialization and ordinal depth supervision, with superior rendering results. Adding 'with Depth Priors' to the title emphasizes an already central component.

C2.justification: v3 adds a depth-distillation interpretation and explicitly discusses consistent depth ordering, rapid-motion pose errors, low-light failures, and failures with more complex motion. It also suggests inverse rendering for specular scenes. Existing explanations and limitations concerning unseen regions, training cost, and depth dependence remain.

D1.justification: A.16 specifies AlexNet for the new LPIPS comparison. A.1 changes the stated 1/5 keyframe sampling to an example without establishing an actual sampling change. The abstract removes the future code-release promise while retaining the project link; the PDFs do not establish changed code availability.

R1.justification: New citations connect MoDGS to video-depth stabilization and distillation, perceptual losses, deblurring, adaptive point fusion, and specular reconstruction. The main related-work narrative remains substantially unchanged. Publication and title updates for existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: v3 updates the title, affiliations, contact information, publication header, and acknowledgments, with localized wording corrections and expanded limitations. A.15–A.20 are appended, but the existing narrative and section organization are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Tables 12–13 and Figures 13–17 substantially expand the visual comparisons for losses, motion, NVDS, and depth estimators. Existing figures remain, with Figure 6 moved alongside Figure 5 and Table 1 repositioned. Conference formatting adds headers and page numbers; Section 3.4 becomes locally crowded.

improvement.justification: The new controlled comparisons in Tables 12–13 strengthen support for ordinal supervision and robustness to depth-prior choice, while expanded limitations clarify applicability. These benefits outweigh minor layout crowding. The overall gain remains limited because the main benchmark evidence is unchanged and the added motion and temporal-stability evidence is qualitative.
